requirement: Describe the Phase I single-dose open-label randomized parallel-group study of DSM265 relative bioavailability and food effect in healthy adults.

evidence.text: The protocol title and synopsis define the study design and objectives.

requirement: Specify random assignment among three regimens: reference DSM265 25% SDD powder fasted, DSM265-TPGS 34% SDD powder fasted, and DSM265-TPGS 34% SDD powder fed.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the three randomized dosing regimens.

requirement: Define PK endpoints including Cmax, Tmax, terminal elimination rate and half-life, AUC to last measurable concentration, AUC0-168, AUC to infinity, and concentration at 168 hours.
Derive DSM265 and applicable metabolite PK parameters by noncompartmental methods from samples collected through 480 hours after dosing.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies PK collection and analysis intent.

requirement: Fit a regimen-effect ANOVA to natural-log Cmax and AUC parameters and back-transform least-squares mean differences to test/reference geometric mean ratios with 90% confidence intervals.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies the model, transformation, and back-transformed intervals.

requirement: Make two planned comparisons: 34% TPGS fasted versus 25% SDD fasted for relative bioavailability, and 34% TPGS fed versus 34% TPGS fasted for food effect.

evidence.text: The SAP defines the two test/reference comparisons.

requirement: Conclude bioequivalence only if the full 90% confidence intervals for the Cmax and AUC geometric mean ratios are within 0.80 to 1.25.

evidence.text: The SAP states the interval containment rule.

requirement: Use 90% confidence intervals for bioavailability equivalence and distinguish them from the nominal 0.05 regimen-effect tests.
Plan 14 participants per regimen, 42 total, as a pragmatic PK and safety sample rather than a formally powered sample.

evidence.text: The SAP states group size and its non-power rationale.

requirement: Use all participants with available data for pharmacokinetic analyses and document any exclusion with a reason.

evidence.text: The SAP defines the PK population and exclusion documentation.

requirement: Define safety analyses to include all participants receiving at least one study-drug dose.

evidence.text: The SAP defines the exposed safety population.

requirement: Normally calculate PK parameters from available concentrations without replacement; permit isolated-sample imputation only when it could materially affect conclusions and document it.
Assess bias from discontinuations potentially related to study drug and use alternative transformations if log-normal assumptions are seriously violated.

evidence.text: The SAP requires missingness-bias review and transformation fallback.

requirement: Summarize treatment-emergent adverse events by regimen, MedDRA SOC and preferred term, severity and relationship, plus laboratory, vital-sign and ECG abnormalities.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies safety domains and counting rules.

requirement: Confirm the precise PK evaluability criteria, handling of below-quantification concentrations, outlier policy, and ANOVA diagnostics before implementation.

evidence.text: The protocol outlines analyses but leaves operational PK rules to the SAP.
